newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico 24, 48-hour pesos end stronger on stocks.
newsitem.headline: Mexico 24, 48-hour pesos end stronger on stocks.

text.p: A rush of funds into Mexico's stock market boosted the peso on Tuesday, switching early declines into gains, dealers said.
"The market was weak this morning on the U.S. long bond then changed to good demand as foreigners entered the market," said one dealer.
The 24-hour peso contract closed up 0.7 of a centavo to 7.4970/7.5010, while the 48-hour spot peso closed up 0.4 of a centavo to 7.5010/7.5050 per dollar.
The Mexican bolsa was up 1.825 percent in late trade.
Dealers added that dollars also entered the market as foreign investors took part in the primary treasury bill auction.
Analyst said that the peso could open stronger on Wednesday if the demand is strong at the T-bill auction, and as the need for dollars for month-end book squaring weakens.
Earlier, the same-day peso contract weakened slightly in early trade, closing down 1.35 centavos to 7.5070/7.5115 per dollar as traders covered positions before the end of the month.
